title: The general confession (1662)
hook: we have left undone those things which we ought to have done
tomorrow: how many things can one thank-you note hold?

segments.voice: That was a week of old books for living: an unsent apology, a teacher past the pages, a room made ready, a heavy box, a morning's thanks, a free lord who serves. Yesterday's line: free, and servant.
screen: `FREE, AND SERVANT.` → `A WEEK OF OLD BOOKS FOR LIVING.`

segments.voice: The obvious place to start an apology is the thing done: the words said, the door slammed. The Book of Common Prayer of 1662 starts somewhere else. Its general confession, meant for everyone in church to say at once, puts this first: "We have left undone those things which we ought to have done." The call that never got made. The question nobody asked. Only after that come the things done.
screen: `START WITH THE THING DONE?` → `THE PRAYER BOOK OF 1662.` → `LEFT UNDONE, FIRST.`

segments.voice: It's called general because nobody says it alone: the whole congregation says it together, after the minister, kneeling. It opens with a picture: "We have erred, and strayed from thy ways like lost sheep." Sheep don't storm off; they wander, one mouthful at a time. Then the two halves, undone and done, and a hard line after them: "And there is no health in us." Then a turn in the grammar. "Spare thou them, O God, which confess their faults." The people have been saying we and us; now they step back and speak of themselves as them, the ones who confess. There's no list of particular sins. Each person brings their own, silently, inside the shared words. Look back over the week and it fits: the Imitation wanted the sorrow, not the definition; Luther gave thanks before asking; the free servant kept no score. Today the prayer book adds the honest list, with the undone things first.
screen: `SAID TOGETHER, KNEELING.` · `LIKE LOST SHEEP.` · `US BECOMES THEM.` · `EACH ONE'S OWN, SILENTLY.` · then, large: `SPARE THOU THEM.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes and let one undone thing come to mind, something small you meant to do and didn't. Don't argue with it or explain it away; just name it honestly. If you pray, you can bring it with the prayer book's own line: spare thou them, O God, which confess their faults.
The general confession. The prayer book's confession for the whole congregation, said together, with each person's own faults held silently inside it.
Your line: spare thou them. The undone things go first on the list. Week done.

screen: `DAY 1645 COUNTS.` → `THE SAINTS IN THEIR OWN WORDS · 44 OF 80.` → `TOMORROW: HOW MANY THINGS CAN ONE THANK-YOU NOTE HOLD?`
